content.tldr: Eric Johnson proposed restructuring engineering reviews into department-specific rotations and simplifying community contribution metrics to a percentage-based KPI. The team also addressed data reporting lags caused by database replication issues and refined bug SLO tracking.

bullets.text: Engineering key reviews will move to a two-month rotation between departments to increase visibility and focus.
The R&D wider MR rate will be replaced by a KPI tracking the percentage of total MRs from the community.
A four-day lag in engineering metrics is being addressed by creating a dedicated database host for the data team.
Bug SLO tracking will shift to focus on the percentage of open bugs exceeding SLOs to prevent metric gaming.
The target for narrow MR rate is officially set to 10 to balance productivity with quality and security goals.
Eric proposed splitting the meeting into four department reviews: Development, Quality, Security, and UX/Infrastructure/Support.
The new format will follow a two-month rotation to avoid adding excessive meetings to stakeholder calendars.
Sid approved the proposal, noting that similar structures are working well in group conversations.
The team clarified that wider MR rate refers specifically to external community contributions per GitLab team member.
Eric and Sid agreed to replace complex taxonomy with a simple percentage of total MRs from the community KPI.
Lily and Mac will manage the transition of these metrics in the reporting dashboards.
Christopher reported that development metrics have not updated for four days due to a data lag issue.
Steve identified the cause as Postgres replication lag on the secondary host used for data pulling.
Infrastructure will create a dedicated host for the data team to eliminate conflicting query traffic.
S1 defect SLO achievement is currently at 80 percent, while S2 achievement is at 60 percent.
Sid requested a new chart showing the percentage of open bugs currently within or outside of SLO.
Mac will work with the data metrics stream to implement tracking for the age of all open bugs.
The narrow MR rate is currently below target due to holidays, vacations, and power outages in Texas.
Christopher expects a performance rebound in March, following historical seasonal trends.
The FY22 target is fixed at 10 to prioritize quality, security, and availability over further productivity increases.
Lily and Mac must transition community contribution metrics to a percentage-based KPI.
Steve will create a dedicated database host for the data engineering team.
Mac will iterate on bug SLO metrics to include the status of open bugs.
Steve will provide an update on database replication issues at the next infrastructure review.

actionItems.text: Work with Max to transition the KPI to percentage of total MRs from the community.
Own escalations for Postgres replication lag and create a dedicated host for the data team to pull from.
Add the Postgres replication issue to the infra key review for next week.
Provide an update on the Postgres replication issue at the infra key review next week.
Perform a deeper dive into the S2 mean time to close spike and provide an update next time.
Take the proposal to measure the percentage of open bugs outside of SLO to the next data metrics work stream.

chapters.title: Meeting Introduction & Agenda Change
chapters.gist: Eric Johnson introduced the meeting and proposed splitting the engineering key review into four department-specific reviews on a two-month rotation to increase visibility and allow deeper dives.

chapters.title: R&D MR Rate KPI Review
chapters.gist: The team discussed the definition and effectiveness of R&D overall and wider MR rates as KPIs, with Eric Johnson proposing a shift to tracking the percentage of total MRs from the community.

chapters.title: Postgres Replication Lag
chapters.gist: Guest 1 raised concerns about Postgres replication lag, its ownership, and potential solutions, with Steve confirming infrastructure's DRI role and plans for a dedicated host.

chapters.title: Defect Tracking & SLOs
chapters.gist: Mac provided an update on defect tracking against SLOs, noting S1s at 80% and S2s at 60%, while Sid critiqued the current measurement method for closed bugs and proposed focusing on open bugs.

chapters.title: Key Metrics & Performance
chapters.gist: The team reviewed overall key metrics, including a smaller decline in SSAT and context on the narrow MR rate, with discussions on historical trends, seasonal dips, and future targets.
